data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's prior year claims development for 2019 and earlier shows a small net release of approximately 8.0 (USD millions), driven by favourable development in older years (notably 2017 and 2018) partially offset by adverse development on 2019. The reserves remain subject to uncertainty due to reliance on cedant bordereaux and external reserving information (notably AXA XL data), IBNR estimation and recoveries from reinsurers.
raw_causal_phrases: This reliance and lack of source data adds an extra layer of uncertainty in relation to estimating claims provisions.
The principal assumption underlying the liability estimates is that the future claims development will follow a similar pattern to past claims development experience.
An element of IBNR also relates to specific large losses, such as catastrophe events.
In 2021, there has been an overall deterioration of GBP 2,626k on prior year reserves (2020: deficit GBP 11,576k).
data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development derived from the gross claims development triangle (pages 43-44). A narrative sentence elsewhere reports a net deterioration in GBP (GBP 2,626k) which appears to be a net (after-reinsurance) figure and in a different currency; the triangle-based gross figure in USD (-8.013m) was used as primary. All monetary figures converted from the report's $'000 units to millions. LOB mapping assigns all reserve movement to Treaty (reinsurance accepted) because the report is a reinsurance-only syndicate and segmental analysis shows only 'Reinsurance accepted'.
